Elaine —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I attached a compact Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft that focuses on the two things you asked for: (1) clear success metrics we can instrument during the pilot and (2) an acceptance cadence tied to a single demo and a short smoke test suite.

High-level summary (see attached HealthSync_MAP_v1.xlsx):
- Success matrix: business KPIs (NPS uplift, triage time reduction), technical SLOs (p95 latency < 450ms, error rate < 0.5%), and quality checks (entity extraction F1 >= 0.82 on the test set).
- Demo acceptance: two-stage demo (stakeholder demo + ops smoke run) with pass/fail gates. If both pass, we consider pilot "accepted" for go/no-go to production.
- Timeline: 4-week pilot, week 3 demo, week 4 acceptance window and remediation.

Action items I propose for next week:
1) You review the metric thresholds and mark any values you want to tighten/loosen.
2) We lock the demo attendee list and demo script (I attached a draft).
3) Sign-off on the MAP (a short DocuSign link included) so we can provision dedicated test capacity.

Attachments: HealthSync_MAP_v1.xlsx (workbook), demo-script.md (outline)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync if you prefer to walk through the spreadsheet.

– Markus Klein

Elaine — quick follow-up from our side. I updated the MAP workbook (attached) with two changes per your ask: switched triage KPI to median and added a "High-risk entity" precision column with threshold 0.90. Also included a short acceptance checklist that maps to our smoke tests.

Acceptance checklist (short version):
- Demo (stakeholder walkthrough): business sign-off recorded in meeting minutes.
- Ops smoke run: 1,000 sample messages processed end-to-end using a shadow dataset; observe run for 48 hours, record p95 latency and errors.
- Quality verification: run the evaluation harness against your labeled 500-example holdout; F1 and precision thresholds must meet the MAP.

If the smoke run or eval harness misses thresholds, we'll run a 72-hour remediation sprint and then re-evaluate. If failures persist, the default is to extend pilot (no automatic production rollout).

Attachments: HealthSync_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated), demo-script.md (annotated)

Markus — I also added a small column to flag whether an acceptance requirement is a "hard gate" (must pass) vs "observation" (informational). Happy to talk through tradeoffs.

- Marissa (Solutions)

Thanks Elaine — quick answers and next steps: 

1) Data handling: we will use a redaction layer for the shadow dataset; PII/PHI fields will be redacted before they enter the test cluster. I'll copy security into a short note and include the retention assumptions you flagged (30 days for logs by default; longer retention available by request and with a contract addendum).

2) Remediation sprint cadence: we propose a defined 72-hour remediation sprint after failed smoke/eval. The sprint includes daily standups with a single technical owner from HealthSync, a Redwood on-call engineer, and a solutions lead. After remediation, we run the same smoke run and evaluation harness; if thresholds still fail we document findings and propose one of: (a) extended pilot with discrete milestones, (b) scoped rollback to a lighter model variant, or (c) stop and revisit scope.

3) Demo invite: propose Thu May 20, 2027 10:00am PT for the stakeholder walkthrough (30 min) and Fri May 21 9:00am PT for the ops smoke run kick-off. I'll send calendars once you confirm attendee list.
